```
Verify each finding against current code. Fix only still-valid issues, skip the
rest with a brief reason, keep changes minimal, and validate.

Inline comments:
In `@lib/widgets/wn_message_bubble.dart`:
- Around line 273-278: The truncated-timestamp path rebuilds plain Text from the
raw string and loses markdown/highlight styling; instead reuse the parsed
TextSpan list produced by _buildMessageTextSpans (textChildren) for both the
TextPainter measurement and the widgets rendered when contentMaxLines overflows.
Update the branches that currently construct Text(content, ...) to accept or
convert textChildren into a RichText/TextSpan-based widget (or to wrap
textChildren in a Text.rich/RichText) so highlightSpans and markdown styling are
preserved during truncation and measurement by TextPainter.

In `@test/widgets/wn_message_bubble_test.dart`:
- Around line 47-88: Add tests covering the truncated/timestamp overflow branch
by mounting WnMessageBubble instances that set timestamp and contentMaxLines so
the widget uses the _TextWithTimestamp overflow path: (1) a case with content
containing markdown markers plus a non-empty timestamp and contentMaxLines small
enough to force truncation to assert the rendered RichText uses the
timestamp/overflow styling, and (2) a case that also supplies highlightSpans
alongside markdown delimiters to verify highlights take precedence over markdown
styling; use the same helpers (_findTextSpan) to assert bold/italic/code styles
or highlighted spans appear as expected in the truncated/timestamp branch.
```

issue.title: fix: reset Whitenoise lifecycle after deleting data
issue.body:
## Description

Fixes the reset lifecycle after deleting all app data.

The bridge now replaces the process-global Whitenoise handle safely: it waits for in-flight bridge calls before closing the old database, clears the global instance after delete, and exposes `reinitializeWhitenoise()` so Flutter can install a fresh instance after the local wipe completes.

Flutter wraps the delete flow with a reset-pending marker. If the app is killed or interrupted during reset, startup recovery clears the local reset surface before initializing Whitenoise again. If deletion succeeds but reinitialization fails in the same process, the app routes to the fatal error flow instead of leaving the user on settings with an uninitialized Rust singleton.

This PR also keeps the start-DM stale-group guard: cached DM group IDs are validated before opening. If the cached group no longer exists in Rust/MDK state, the app falls back to creating a fresh DM instead of failing with `Group not found`.

This app-side lifecycle fix depends on the companion `whitenoise-rs` bounded-delete PR, which prevents local data deletion from hanging behind stuck scheduler/background/relay shutdown work:

https://github.com/marmot-protocol/whitenoise-rs/pull/840

Closes #660

## Type of Change

- [ ] ✨ New feature (non-breaking change which adds functionality)
- [x] 🛠️ Bug fix (non-breaking change which fixes an issue)
- [ ] ❌ Breaking change (fix or feature that would cause existing functionality to change)
- [ ] 🧹 Code refactor
- [ ] ✅ Build configuration change
- [ ] 📝 Documentation
- [ ] 🗑️ Chore
- [x] 🧪 Tests

## How I Tested This

- `cargo test --locked`
- `just precommit` passes.
- Ran the app on my phone, created chats, sent messages, deleted app data, and logged in again.
- After deleting app data and logging in again, searched for a user and started a DM without hitting the stale `Group not found` path.

## Screenshots

Not applicable; no UI layout changes.

issue.body: ## Description Completes the block/unblock feature with the two missing pieces: 1. **Hide the chat composer when the peer is blocked.** The "You blocked this user" banner already rendered in chats; only the input gate was missing. 2. **Settings → Privacy & Security → Blocked users.** A list of all blocked accounts, tap a row to open a profile-detail modal with an Unblock action. The detail opens over a blurred list following the existing `chat_info_screen` pattern (`opaque: false` + `WnOverlay(light)`). Reuses existing hooks (`useBlockActions`, `useBlockedPubkeys`, `useUserMetadata`, `useRouteRefresh`) and shared widgets (`WnSlate`, `WnOverlay`, `WnChatInfoProfileCard`, `WnUserItem`). No Rust changes. **Architectural note:** `BlockedUsersScreen`'s `WnSlate` uses a unique Hero tag (`'blocked-users-list-slate'`). `chat_info_screen` keeps the chat content visible behind by placing the message list *outside* its slate; the mock for this feature requires the list *inside* the slate, so the source-only tag asymmetry is the minimum-deviation way to keep the list visible behind the detail modal. ## Type of Change - [x] ✨ New feature (non-breaking change which adds functionality) - [ ] 🛠️ Bug fix - [ ] ❌ Breaking change - [ ] 🧹 Code refactor - [ ] ✅ Build configuration change - [ ] 📝 Documentation - [ ] 🗑️ Chore - [ ] 🧪 Tests ## How I Tested This - **Pixel 9 Pro XL** (Android, physical device, arm64-v8a): full walkthrough — block a peer in chat → composer hides → Settings → Privacy → View blocked users → tap a row → modal-over-blurred-list renders → tap Unblock → list refreshes via `useRouteRefresh` on pop. - **Pixel_9_Pro AVD** (Android emulator, x86_64, Android 16): clean install + boot to login splash on a fresh AVD, same process as above. Test suite: 4489/4489 pass. Coverage 99.40% global, 100% on the two new screens. `just precommit` green across all 9 gates. ## Screenshots UI changes - Settings → Privacy & Security with the new "Blocked users" section - Blocked users list - Blocked user profile detail (modal over blurred list) - Chat with a blocked peer (composer hidden, banner visible) ## Checklist - [x] `just precommit` passes - [x] `CHANGELOG.md` updated - [x] Screenshots added ## Summary by CodeRabbit * **Documentation** * Updated changelog noting the blocked-users feature. * **New Features** * Added Blocked Users management under Settings → Privacy & Security. * View blocked-users list, open blocked-user profiles, and unblock users. * Chat composer/input is hidden when a peer is blocked. * **Localization** * Added translations for the blocked-users UI across multiple languages. * **Tests** * Added widget tests covering blocked-users screens, unblock flows, and related UI states. issue.title: feat(blocked-users): complete block/unblock UX
issue.body: ## Description Completes the block/unblock feature with the two missing pieces: 1. **Hide the chat composer when the peer is blocked.** The "You blocked this user" banner already rendered in chats; only the input gate was missing. 2. **Settings → Privacy & Security → Blocked users.** A list of all blocked accounts, tap a row to open a profile-detail modal with an Unblock action. The detail opens over a blurred list following the existing `chat_info_screen` pattern (`opaque: false` + `WnOverlay(light)`). Reuses existing hooks (`useBlockActions`, `useBlockedPubkeys`, `useUserMetadata`, `useRouteRefresh`) and shared widgets (`WnSlate`, `WnOverlay`, `WnChatInfoProfileCard`, `WnUserItem`). No Rust changes. **Architectural note:** `BlockedUsersScreen`'s `WnSlate` uses a unique Hero tag (`'blocked-users-list-slate'`). `chat_info_screen` keeps the chat content visible behind by placing the message list *outside* its slate; the mock for this feature requires the list *inside* the slate, so the source-only tag asymmetry is the minimum-deviation way to keep the list visible behind the detail modal. ## Type of Change - [x] ✨ New feature (non-breaking change which adds functionality) - [ ] 🛠️ Bug fix - [ ] ❌ Breaking change - [ ] 🧹 Code refactor - [ ] ✅ Build configuration change - [ ] 📝 Documentation - [ ] 🗑️ Chore - [ ] 🧪 Tests ## How I Tested This - **Pixel 9 Pro XL** (Android, physical device, arm64-v8a): full walkthrough — block a peer in chat → composer hides → Settings → Privacy → View blocked users → tap a row → modal-over-blurred-list renders → tap Unblock → list refreshes via `useRouteRefresh` on pop. - **Pixel_9_Pro AVD** (Android emulator, x86_64, Android 16): clean install + boot to login splash on a fresh AVD, same process as above. Test suite: 4489/4489 pass. Coverage 99.40% global, 100% on the two new screens. `just precommit` green across all 9 gates. ## Screenshots UI changes - Settings → Privacy & Security with the new "Blocked users" section - Blocked users list - Blocked user profile detail (modal over blurred list) - Chat with a blocked peer (composer hidden, banner visible) ## Checklist - [x] `just precommit` passes - [x] `CHANGELOG.md` updated - [x] Screenshots added ## Summary by CodeRabbit * **Documentation** * Updated changelog noting the blocked-users feature. * **New Features** * Added Blocked Users management under Settings → Privacy & Security. * View blocked-users list, open blocked-user profiles, and unblock users. * Chat composer/input is hidden when a peer is blocked. * **Localization** * Added translations for the blocked-users UI across multiple languages. * **Tests** * Added widget tests covering blocked-users screens, unblock flows, and related UI states. > 🤖 `_isMentionBoundary` only accepts whitespace, so `@npub1...!` will refuse to auto-truncate. The Rust parser is more permissive.
> *How to address:* extend `_isMentionBoundary` to also accept `.`, `,`, `;`, `:`, `!`, `?`, `)`, `]`. Add tests.

🤖 Agent concern
> **Image alt-text and code-block previews are unbounded** (`markdown_text.dart:478-484`, `:63-68`).
> A peer can send `![](url) alt=<10 KB>`, which renders as `[image: <10 KB>]` in the bubble; `firstParagraphInlines` will also lift a code-block's first line into the reply preview verbatim. Both are abusable for visual DoS (an oversized preview row breaking the chat list).
> *How to address:* truncate alt text to ~100 chars before rendering (`markdown_text.dart:478`). In `_firstNonEmptyLine` (`:85`), cap to ~120 chars and add an ellipsis. Add a test with 10 KB alt text.

My agent raised this concern here 🤖 
> **`MarkdownText` `TapGestureRecognizer`s can leak past widget unmount** (`markdown_text.dart:122-141`).
> Stale recognizers from the previous build are disposed via `WidgetsBinding.instance.addPostFrameCallback`. If the widget is removed before the next frame (Navigator.pop during scroll, hot reload, fast list rebuild), the callback still runs but the recognizers held callbacks that captured `BuildContext` and closures referencing now-disposed objects.
> *How to address:* dispose stale recognizers **synchronously** at the start of `build` before reassigning `activeRecognizers.value`. Add a leak test that pumps the widget, unmounts, and asserts no listener leak (`leak_tracker`).

My agent raised this 🤖 

> `_shiftPastReplacements` uses the wrong "old length"** (`mention_text_editing_controller.dart:403-430`).
> The helper computes `oldRangeLen = r.uri.length`, but `r` is a `_TrackedMention` whose `uri` is the *bare npub* form (`@npub1…`, ~63 chars). When called from `_replaceBareNpubs` this is correct *by coincidence*; when called from `_replaceKnownUris` (`:327`), `r.uri` is the picker URI (e.g. `@npub1alice...`) but the **old** text contained `@DisplayName` (display text from a previous resolver pass). With short display names this currently produces a correct delta because both writers happen to use `uri.length` as old, but if a future caller registers a target where `displayText.length > uri.length`, surviving mentions are silently dropped.
> *How to address:* change `_shiftPastReplacements` to take `(oldStart, oldEnd, newStart, newEnd)` tuples instead of reconstructing from `_TrackedMention`. Add a test where `displayText.length > uri.length`.

`@dannym-arx`, the Comment image makes it clear — mentions render as bold text in the per-pubkey avatar color with no underline, which looks clean and intentional. Withdrawing my suggestion; the current `_mentionStyle` implementation is correct per Vlad's design direction.

issue.title: fix: reset Whitenoise lifecycle after deleting data
issue.body:
## Description

Fixes the reset lifecycle after deleting all app data.

The bridge now replaces the process-global Whitenoise handle safely: it waits for in-flight bridge calls before closing the old database, clears the global instance after delete, and exposes `reinitializeWhitenoise()` so Flutter can install a fresh instance after the local wipe completes.

Flutter wraps the delete flow with a reset-pending marker. If the app is killed or interrupted during reset, startup recovery clears the local reset surface before initializing Whitenoise again. If deletion succeeds but reinitialization fails in the same process, the app routes to the fatal error flow instead of leaving the user on settings with an uninitialized Rust singleton.

This PR also keeps the start-DM stale-group guard: cached DM group IDs are validated before opening. If the cached group no longer exists in Rust/MDK state, the app falls back to creating a fresh DM instead of failing with `Group not found`.

This app-side lifecycle fix depends on the companion `whitenoise-rs` bounded-delete PR, which prevents local data deletion from hanging behind stuck scheduler/background/relay shutdown work:

https://github.com/marmot-protocol/whitenoise-rs/pull/840

Closes #660

## Type of Change

- [ ] ✨ New feature (non-breaking change which adds functionality)
- [x] 🛠️ Bug fix (non-breaking change which fixes an issue)
- [ ] ❌ Breaking change (fix or feature that would cause existing functionality to change)
- [ ] 🧹 Code refactor
- [ ] ✅ Build configuration change
- [ ] 📝 Documentation
- [ ] 🗑️ Chore
- [x] 🧪 Tests

## How I Tested This

- `cargo test --locked`
- `just precommit` passes.
- Ran the app on my phone, created chats, sent messages, deleted app data, and logged in again.
- After deleting app data and logging in again, searched for a user and started a DM without hitting the stale `Group not found` path.

## Screenshots

Not applicable; no UI layout changes.

- [x] `just precommit` passes
- [x] Related issue linked (`Closes #660`)
- [x] `CHANGELOG.md` updated (if user-visible change)

issue.body:
![marmot](https://blossom.primal.net/35d671f7406873029a2b8cd5e12660eb6642cb3cdbe841a429ae0e94f0d43bff.png)


https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/813ae5ee-daef-4bdf-aec6-cd0f390a2198



> Heads up: most of the diff is FRB codegen. Net total is ~7800 added lines; ~4300 of that is autogenerated `lib/src/rust/` and `rust/src/frb_generated.rs`, regenerated whenever the bridge surface changes. The hand-written review surface is ~1500 lines plus ~1700 lines of tests. Skim the codegen, read the rest.

This PR consumes the new `whitenoise_markdown::Document` AST from whitenoise-rs (pinned at `f421a8ad`). Chat bubbles now render CommonMark, GFM, and the nostr-extension format. Plain-text messages render byte-identically to before.

The marmots have learned to read bold text.

## What's in here

- `WnMarkdownText` walks the parsed AST and renders every Block and Inline variant.
- Plain-text fast path: single-paragraph messages with only Text/SoftBreak/HardBreak inlines skip the markdown renderer entirely. They keep the existing inline-timestamp layout.
- `@npub` mentions render as underlined `@DisplayName` (Vlad's design call). Tap opens a new in-app `UserProfileShade` instead of bouncing out to the OS. Non-npub Nostr URIs (note, nevent, nprofile, naddr, nrelay) still route externally because they point at events, not people.
- `SoftBreak` renders as a newline. The CommonMark default is a space, which loses every Enter press in the composer.
- URL scheme allow-list: `http`, `https`, `mailto`, `nostr`, `tel`. Anything else gets no tap recognizer at the renderer layer; the bubble's tap handler reapplies the same check before `launchUrl`. The Rust parser does not recognize HTML, so `<script>` and similar pass through as literal text.
- Surface boundaries: chat-list previews, reply quotes, notifications, and the composer keep their existing plain-text rendering.

## Bridge style

The bridge mirrors each AST type through FRB. The AST is FRB-friendly: owned `String`, `Vec<Enum>` recursion, `Clone`, `Eq`. Generated Dart sealed classes give exhaustive switch and IDE help. A hand-rolled Dart JSON parser would be a second markdown implementation and would drift from upstream.

## Tests + manual QA

- 4498 Flutter tests + 75 Rust tests pass. Coverage 99.03%. `just precommit` clean.
- Manual checklist run locally: every Block and Inline variant, surface boundaries, security cases (`javascript:`, `data:`, raw HTML stay inert), nested containers, CJK and RTL mixed runs, mention-tap into shade and back without scroll jump, long-press preview shows resolved names.

## Known limitations

1. Cross-inline highlight matches are not highlighted in search results.
2. Math renders as italic monospace source; no LaTeX engine is used.
3. Inline markdown images render as `[image: alt]` text links, not embedded.
4. Mentions of users outside the chat's metadata cache fall back to truncated npub until metadata loads. Follow-up could subscribe to mentioned pubkeys.

## Incidental upstream commits

The rev bump pulled in two non-markdown commits: `917ad14` (handle_contact_list lock contention) and `585d31f` (MDK update + push-token gossip). Both required adding `disappearing_message_secs: None` to two struct literals in `rust/src/api/groups.rs`.

  * In-chat mention suggestions with resolved display names and insertion support
  * Tappable links and Nostr mentions with safe handling and in-app navigation (including opening profiles/chats)

* **UX Improvements**
  * Quoted-message previews render Markdown when available
  * Start-chat can open as a non-opaque “shade” for smoother flows

* **Localization**

```
echo "===== wn_message_bubble.dart _timestampReservedWidth + _shouldRenderAsMarkdown ====="

grep -n 'set value\|_remap\|_tracked\|messageText\|insertMention\|_replaceBare' lib/utils/mention_text_editing_controller.dart | head -60
```

Length of output: 18855

---



</details>

The PR description image shows the cozy pixel-art marmot in a knit sweater at a retro desk, scroll in hand with "**bold**" and "+italic+", chat bubbles calling out `# heading`, `@mention`, two `code block` labels, and a bullet list — a fitting hero for a markdown feature.

---

`@dannym-arx` — here's the golden carrot 🥕

## The Golden Carrot: `_timestampReservedWidth` ignores text scaling, breaking the plain-text fast path for accessibility users

**File:** `lib/widgets/wn_message_bubble.dart` — `_timestampReservedWidth` (line 304)

### What the code says

Every other `TextPainter` in `_TextWithTimestamp` correctly reads both `Directionality` and `textScaler` from context:

```dart
// ✅ Lines 134–153 — correctly scaled painters already in the same widget
final painter = TextPainter(
  text: ...,
  textDirection: Directionality.of(context),   // ← present
  textScaler: MediaQuery.textScalerOf(context), // ← present
)..layout();
```

But `_timestampReservedWidth` — the function responsible for punching out space so the timestamp never overlaps the message text — does **not** pass either:

```dart
// ❌ Line 304 — the offending function
double _timestampReservedWidth(
  String timestamp,
  TextStyle tsStyle,
  bool isOutgoing,
  bool showDeliveryStatus,
) {
  final painter = TextPainter(
    text: TextSpan(text: timestamp, style: tsStyle),
    textDirection: TextDirection.ltr, // ← hard-coded, ignores locale
    // ← textScaler entirely absent → always measures at scale 1.0
  );
```

### Why this PR makes it the single biggest issue

Before this PR, there was one code path for all messages. Now `_shouldRenderAsMarkdown` (line 430) splits rendering in two:

```mermaid
flowchart TD
    A[Message] --> B{isPlainTextDocument?}
    B -- "yes (vast majority)" --> C[_TextWithTimestamp\n→ _timestampReservedWidth ❌ scale=1.0]
    B -- "no (formatted)" --> D[MarkdownText + separate timestamp row\n✅ correctly laid out]
```

The **markdown path** is fine. The **plain-text fast path** — which handles the overwhelming majority of all messages — is permanently routed through `_timestampReservedWidth`, which computes reserved width at scale 1.0. At iOS Dynamic Type "Accessibility Large" or Android font scale ≥ 1.3, the timestamp string is wider than the reserved slot, and it **physically overlaps the last word of every plain-text message**. That's a concrete, visible defect for every user who bumps their font size — and it will fail App Store accessibility review.

### The fix (mechanical, four lines)

```diff
 double _timestampReservedWidth(
+  BuildContext context,
   String timestamp,
   TextStyle tsStyle,
   bool isOutgoing,
   bool showDeliveryStatus,
 ) {
   final painter = TextPainter(
     text: TextSpan(text: timestamp, style: tsStyle),
-    textDirection: TextDirection.ltr,
+    textDirection: Directionality.of(context),
+    textScaler: MediaQuery.textScalerOf(context),
   );
```

And at the call site (line 98):

```diff
-    final reservedWidth = _timestampReservedWidth(
+    final reservedWidth = _timestampReservedWidth(
+      context,
       timestamp,
       tsStyle,
       isOutgoing,
       showDeliveryStatus,
     );
```

### Why this beats the other candidates

| Issue | Scope | Severity |
|---|---|---|
| **`_timestampReservedWidth` no textScaler** ← golden carrot | Every plain-text message (majority) | Visual defect at a11y font sizes; App Store risk |
| Recognizer `useRef` accumulation between dep-unchanged rebuilds | Only messages with links/mentions | Memory leak only; stale recognizers are orphaned from TextSpan tree so they can't fire |
| `_shiftMentions` IME edge cases | CJK/IME input only | Mention silently dropped; narrow user segment |
| Mention `_mentionStyle` missing underline | Mentions only | Style spec mismatch; cosmetic |

Fix the timestamp reserved width before merging — everything else can be follow-up issues.

🐇

_⚠️ Potential issue_ | _🟠 Major_ | _⚡ Quick win_

<details>
<summary>🧩 Analysis chain</summary>

🌐 Web query:

`In Dart, for a Directory URI ending with a trailing slash, can `entity.uri.pathSegments.last` be an empty string?`

💡 Result:

Yes, in Dart, if a URI path ends with a trailing slash, the last element of the pathSegments list will be an empty string [1][2]. According to the URI specification (RFC 3986), a path ending in a slash is interpreted as having an empty segment at the end [2]. Dart's Uri class follows this convention: when you access the pathSegments property, the path is split by the slash character, and a trailing slash results in an empty string as the final element in the returned list [1]. For example, for a URI like 'https://example.com/folder/', the pathSegments property will return ['folder', '']. Consequently, accessing.last on this list will yield an empty string [1].

Citations:

- 1: https://github.com/dart-lang/sdk/issues/56735
- 2: https://stackoverflow.com/questions/61547014/restful-uri-trailing-slash-or-no-trailing-slash
